culture.textEn: Jirisan became Korea's first national park in 1967. Today Korea has 24 national parks, and most of them are mountain parks.

sources.title: 우리나라 국립공원
sources.quoteOrLocator: ‘1967년 국립공원위원회의 공원지정 결의와 국토종합계획심의회 통과 후 지리산을 제 1호 국립공원으로 지정’ / ‘현재 24개의 국립공원이 지정·관리되고 있습니다.’ / ‘전국 24개 국립공원은 유형에 따라 산악형 19개, 해상·해안형 4개, 사적형 1개’ / ‘국립공원을 찾는 탐방객수는 연간 4천 3백만 명에 달합니다.(2025년 기준)’

sources.title: 지리산서 태백산까지… 반세기 만에 완성한 국립공원
sources.publisher: 국가기록원 (National Archives of Korea) — 기록으로 만나는 대한민국
sources.quoteOrLocator: ‘우리나라 국립공원 제1호는 … 지리산이다.’ / ‘1967년 12월 27일 국토건설종합계획 심의회를 통과함에 따라 12월 29일 지리산이 우리나라 최초의 국립공원으로 지정되었다.’ (its count of 22 parks is as of July 2016; today's 24 is the Korea National Park Service's)

verification.notes:
Pass 1 (author sourcing, CM-3C, 2026-10-23): the Korea National Park Service page 우리나라 국립공원 says Jirisan was named the first national park in 1967, that 24 national parks are named today, and that 19 of them are mountain parks. 'Today' is as of the access date. English paraphrase.
Pass 1b (second source, 2026-10-23): the National Archives of Korea theme page on national parks says Jirisan was named Korea's first national park on 29 December 1967.
Pass 2 (fact check, 2026-10-23): page fetched again (it needs a browser user agent); 1967, 제 1호, 24개 and 산악형 19개 found. Claim holds.
Pass 3 (MAR checklist pass by the authoring agent, 2026-10-23): F-CURR-002 §5.1 conventions (institution named as on the access date, no UNESCO claim beyond the exact element, shared East Asian heritage not framed as Korean in origin), §7.7 checklist (no age wording, no emoji, no speaking UI, neutral tone) and the 해요체 of the tokens checked. Pass. The independent MAR culture review re-runs in the PR review stage.
Pass 4 (independent MAR culture, facts and language review, a reviewer agent other than the author, 2026-10-23): Korea National Park Service 우리나라 국립공원 re-read: '현재 24개의 국립공원', Jirisan the first (1967), 19 of the 24 are mountain parks. Holds. es/ko checked.

culture.textEn: Korea's national parks are places to rest in nature. In 2025 they counted about 43 million visitors.

sources.title: 우리나라 국립공원
sources.quoteOrLocator: ‘1967년 국립공원위원회의 공원지정 결의와 국토종합계획심의회 통과 후 지리산을 제 1호 국립공원으로 지정’ / ‘현재 24개의 국립공원이 지정·관리되고 있습니다.’ / ‘전국 24개 국립공원은 유형에 따라 산악형 19개, 해상·해안형 4개, 사적형 1개’ / ‘국립공원을 찾는 탐방객수는 연간 4천 3백만 명에 달합니다.(2025년 기준)’

sources.title: 국립공원 탐방객 증가 추세 이어져… 2025년 4,331만 명… 전년 대비 6.5% 증가
sources.quoteOrLocator: 보도자료 제목 (2026.02.24): ‘국립공원 탐방객 증가 추세 이어져… 2025년 4,331만 명…’

verification.notes:
Pass 1 (author sourcing, CM-3C, 2026-10-23): the same Korea National Park Service page calls the parks the public's place of rest (국민의 휴식처) and gives about 43 million visitors a year, counted for 2025. English paraphrase.
Pass 1b (second source, 2026-10-23): the ministry press release on korea.kr (24 February 2026) gives 43.31 million national park visitors in 2025.
Pass 2 (fact check, 2026-10-23): page fetched again; 휴식처 and 4천 3백만 명 (2025년 기준) found. Claim holds.
Pass 3 (MAR checklist pass by the authoring agent, 2026-10-23): F-CURR-002 §5.1 conventions (institution named as on the access date, no UNESCO claim beyond the exact element, shared East Asian heritage not framed as Korean in origin), §7.7 checklist (no age wording, no emoji, no speaking UI, neutral tone) and the 해요체 of the tokens checked. Pass. The independent MAR culture review re-runs in the PR review stage.
Pass 4 (independent MAR culture, facts and language review, a reviewer agent other than the author, 2026-10-23): KNPS page and the korea.kr release of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment re-read: '2025년 4,331만 명'; 'about 43 million' holds. es/ko checked.

culture.textEn: The Asiatic black bear, {ko:반달가슴곰}, became endangered in Korea. In 2004 a project began in Jirisan National Park to help the bears live there again.

sources.title: 반달가슴곰
sources.quoteOrLocator: ‘한반도 전역에 서식하던 반달가슴곰은 … 멸종위기에 처해 있으며 2004년 지리산국립공원에서 복원사업이 시작되었습니다.’

sources.title: 반달가슴곰 복원 20주년, ‘공존(共存): 사람과 자연의 동행’
sources.publisher: 기후에너지환경부 (발표 당시 환경부) 보도자료 — 대한민국 정책브리핑 (korea.kr)
sources.quoteOrLocator: 보도자료 제목 (2024.10.29, 환경부): ‘반달가슴곰 복원 20주년’, twenty years from the 2004 start the Korea National Park Service page gives

verification.notes:
Pass 1 (author sourcing, CM-3C, 2026-10-23): the Korea National Park Service page 반달가슴곰 says the bear, once found across the peninsula, is endangered, and that the restoration project began in Jirisan National Park in 2004. The causes the page lists are left out (child-safe tone). English paraphrase.
Pass 1b (second source, 2026-10-23): the Ministry of Environment press release on korea.kr (29 October 2024) marks 20 years of the bear restoration, which matches the 2004 start.
Pass 2 (fact check, 2026-10-23): page fetched again; 멸종위기 and 2004년 지리산국립공원에서 복원사업 found. Claim holds.
Pass 3 (MAR checklist pass by the authoring agent, 2026-10-23): F-CURR-002 §5.1 conventions (institution named as on the access date, no UNESCO claim beyond the exact element, shared East Asian heritage not framed as Korean in origin), §7.7 checklist (no age wording, no emoji, no speaking UI, neutral tone) and the 해요체 of the tokens checked. Pass. The independent MAR culture review re-runs in the PR review stage.
Pass 4 (independent MAR culture, facts and language review, a reviewer agent other than the author, 2026-10-23): KNPS 반달가슴곰 re-read: endangered, restoration begun in Jirisan National Park in 2004. Holds. The second source's publisher now names the ministry as on the access date (기후에너지환경부, then 환경부; reorganised October 2025). es/ko checked.

notes: Language and translation passes 4 and 6 (MAR, #637): no distractor borrows a sibling cell's Discover item; q2 asks only its own words; ko glosses are definitions with no echo (가겠다고 대답하는 말, 공원으로 간다는 대답); the q1 Story Sequence keeps speaker turns; es names no gendered friend; romanization follows checkRomanization.

Culture pass 5 (MAR, #637): no culture claim and no sourced language note (culture: []), so no verification record; no real person, shop, brand or price; no age wording; the friend is never gendered in es.

CM-3C (F-CURR-002 §5.5 S4, 2026-10-23): culture notes n1-n3 added (Jirisan the first national park, 1967; 24 parks; visitors; the Asiatic black bear project), source Korea National Park Service, each with its own verification record.

Culture notes (CM-3C, MAR 2026-10-23): an independent reviewer agent re-read every source of the new notes (all §6.6 hosts, the allowlisted one first), checked §5.1 and §7.7 and the es and ko overlays; findings applied. No native-speaker or expert review is claimed.

Check rotation MAR (row CM-3A S4, F-CURR-002 section 7.1, 2026-10-27; passes: language, culture and facts, learning design, reviser, third pass): Nature plays Tap to Respond and Realia Read on a weather card (four rounds, every answer an entry of the card); the Checks are Cloze Pick, Sentence Builder and Cloze Pick.

CM-3A S4 MAR (cont.): Language: 비가, 날씨가 after a vowel, 집에 and 공원에 for where to; the weather words on the cards (해, 비, 구름, 바람) and places (공원, 산, 바다, 강) are taught topic words. Culture and facts: the weather cards are made-up park forecasts, no real data; the CM-3C park notes are unchanged.

CM-3A S4 MAR (cont.): Learning design: the Checks complete the Discover lines, so the cell adds only its cards and the word 내일. Reviser and third pass: es and ko glosses checked; no native-speaker or expert review is claimed.
CM-3A S4 review fix (2026-10-27): the ko gloss of the q3 Check's first Cloze round names the park (공원으로 간다는 말), so the gap is decided by its meaning, not by a word echoed in a tile gloss.
